tip: "Tout va bien" is literally "everything goes well" – French checks how things are with aller (to go), not être (to be). Same verb hides in Comment ça va ?
French makes grooming verbs reflexive: elle se maquille is literally "she makes herself up." The se points the action back on her – no English "herself" needed.
French doesn't "agree" with a verb – you ARE in agreement: être d'accord. Je suis d'accord = literally "I am of agreement."
"dix-huit heures" = 18:00. France runs on the 24-hour clock for schedules, so 6pm becomes eighteen hundred: dix-huit heures, not six heures.
"cinq heures moins le quart" is "five hours minus the quarter" = 4:45. Before the hour French subtracts: moins le quart = quarter to.
"tout le monde" literally means "all the world," but it just means everyone: elle a dit bonjour à tout le monde = she said hi to everybody.
"faire les courses" isn't running races – here courses means errands, and faire (to make/do) covers shopping: tu as fait les courses = did you do the shopping.
French uses the plain article for body parts, not "their": elles ont ouvert les yeux = they opened the eyes, meaning their own. Ownership is understood.
"Ça ne fait rien" is literally "that does nothing" = no worries / it doesn't matter. The ne...rien pair wraps the verb to mean "nothing."
